guide.title: Student guide: submitting your group project
guide.leaderWarning: IMPORTANT: ONLY THE GROUP LEAD SHOULD DO THIS STEP. The person who creates the group is automatically added as the leader, and every teammate you add joins that group. If another member creates a separate group, your team will be split up.

select.title: 1. Open the project dashboard
select.alt: Projects page with the DUMMY PROJECT dashboard title highlighted
select.body:
Open Projects from the left sidebar. The page lists the project dashboards your TA has posted for your courses.

Click the highlighted project title (for example DUMMY PROJECT) to open its dashboard. The card also shows the section, the team size and the final deadline — check the deadline before you start.

group.title: 2. Create your group
group.alt: Create your group form with the project title field, leader card and teammate drop-down highlighted
group.body:
Enter a project title, then pick your teammates from the drop-down. Only students currently enrolled in your section appear in the list.

Press Add after each selection and check the member count line (for example “2 of 5 members selected”). When the group is complete, press Create group. The Group ID (for example DUM_1_01) is generated automatically.
group.highlight: The teammate drop-down and the “Create group” button.

details.title: 3. Fill in the project details
details.alt: My group page with the member list, status badges and the project details fields
details.body:
After creating the group you land on My group. The header shows your Group ID and two badges — the dashboard status and your submission status. Members are listed at the top with the leader marked.

Scroll to Project details and fill every field that has a red asterisk (*): project title, project idea/description, problem statement and proposed solution. Paste your GitHub repository link in the Github Repo Link field — it must start with https://. Use the optional Project links rows for demos, documents or extra repositories.
details.highlight: Every field marked with a red * is required.

submit.title: 4. Submit your project
submit.alt: Submission form with the Submit project button highlighted
submit.body:
Check every required field once more. When the form is complete, press the highlighted Submit project button.

Your work is saved as a version — the version number and submission time appear under the button. If your TA allows edits after submission, or asks for changes, you can edit the form and submit again; each save becomes a new version.

verify.title: 5. Verify that the submission was recorded
verify.alt: Projects page showing the group under My project groups with a Submitted badge
verify.body:
You are taken back to Projects. Under My project groups your group now shows the Submitted badge next to its Group ID.

If the badge still says Not submitted, your work was not recorded — open My group and submit again. Use the My group button any time to reopen your submission, links and TA feedback.
verify.highlight: The Submitted badge and the My group button.

Home.heroTitle: Your whole course, in one calm place.
Home.heroBody: Marks, evaluation bookings, schedules and announcements — finally together, so you can stop digging through chats and spreadsheets.
Home.heroNote: Free for students. Sign in with your university account.
Home.previewFooter: Everything updates from one source of truth.
Home.featuresTitle: Built for the way your term actually runs
Home.featuresBody: No more decoding screenshots of spreadsheets or scrolling a group chat for one date.
Home.featureMarks: See released marks per assessment, with a weighted marksheet and class statistics.
Home.featureBooking: Reserve evaluation slots with live capacity, and cancel before the cutoff.
Home.featureAnnouncements: Course announcements from your teaching staff land in one place.
Home.featureAnalytics: Weighted totals and distribution insights, with small groups suppressed for privacy.
Home.stepsBody: Metria mirrors how a course actually runs — a term, a set of offerings, sections, assessments and the people enrolled in them.
Home.stepOneBody: Your enrolled course is the front door: marks, schedule and staff announcements in one view.
Home.stepTwoTitle: Check marks and book a slot
Home.stepTwoBody: Marks are entered once and flow everywhere. Evaluation bookings show live seats, so there is no guessing.
Home.stepThreeBody: Announcements and upcoming assessments arrive on your dashboard — no group-chat archaeology needed.
Home.audienceBody: Everyone sees exactly what they need — and nothing they do not.
Home.audienceStudentBody: Marks, marksheet, bookings and course announcements.
Home.audienceTaBody: Sections, marks entry and live evaluation capacity.
Home.audienceStaffBody: Distribution and per-section analytics, with small groups suppressed.
Home.trustTitle: Private by default, not by promise
Home.trustBody: Access rules live in the database, not just in the interface. A student sees their own marks and bookings; staff see only the sections they manage; platform administrators are audited.
Home.trustPointOne: Row-level access enforced in the database
Home.trustPointTwo: Small class groups suppressed in analytics
Home.trustPointThree: Ads never on the sign-in or admin screens
Home.adsNoteBody: Metria is free for students, and a few sponsored tabs help keep it that way. Every now and then, a click may open a sponsored tab behind this one — at most 4 times a day, then it stops for a while.
Home.adsNoteTipBefore: The trick: for those first few clicks, keep a finger on
Home.adsNoteTipAfter: If a tab opens behind you, this closes it instantly and you are back here — nothing to read, nothing to scroll. On a Mac, use ⌘ + W instead.
Home.finalBody: Sign in with your university Google account and pick up where your course left off.
Home.finalNote: For students, teaching assistants and course staff.

about.title: About
about.intro: {product} is a university academic workspace for marks, evaluation bookings and course announcements.
about.mission: Course administration is usually spread across spreadsheets, chat groups and paper sign-up sheets. Metria puts the same information in one place, visible only to the people who are allowed to see it.
about.audience: Students, teaching assistants and course staff at a university. The first tenant is FAST-NUCES Lahore; each university is a separate tenant with its own data.
about.privacy: Access is enforced in the database, not just the interface. Small class groups are suppressed in analytics so individual marks cannot be inferred from statistics.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: {product} collects the minimum needed to run your courses: your university account identity, your memberships and roles, and the academic records for the courses you are enrolled in or staff.
privacy.collect: Your name and email from your university Google account, your tenant membership, and course data such as assessments, marks, evaluation bookings and announcements. We do not sell personal data.
privacy.ads: Public pages and the authenticated app may show advertising served by third-party advertising networks. These networks may use cookies and similar technologies to measure and personalise advertising. Advertising networks are listed in our ad configuration and are subject to their own privacy policies. Some advertising, including popunder ads, may open a sponsored page in a new tab after you interact with a page; we try to keep the current page focused, but browser tab-focus rules vary.
privacy.adsNetworks: The advertising networks currently approved for this site are Adsterra and HilltopAds. Advertising scripts load only after you grant consent for the advertising category. Popunder ads are limited to four sponsored-tab opens every 24 hours; a first-party cookie stores only a random browser id and recent open times to enforce that limit. No fingerprinting is used.
privacy.consent: Non-essential scripts, including advertising, do not load until you accept them in the consent banner. You can reject non-essential categories and still use the site. Your choice is stored in a first-party cookie.
privacy.app: Advertising may appear inside the authenticated application, including the dashboard, course, marks and booking pages. Third-party advertising scripts load only after you grant consent. On the detailed marksheet, sensitive mark values stay behind tap-to-reveal while advertising is active.
privacy.contact: For privacy questions or data requests, contact the team using the address on the contact page.

terms.title: Terms of Use
terms.intro: By using {product} you agree to these terms. If you do not agree, do not use the service.
terms.accounts: Access is limited to members of a participating university. You must use your own university account and keep your credentials secure. Accounts may be suspended for misuse.
terms.use: Do not attempt to access data you are not authorised to see, disrupt the service, scrape it at scale, or use it to harass other users. Academic records must be used only for their intended purpose.
terms.content: Course content, marks and announcements belong to the university and the people who created them. You may not redistribute other users' data.
terms.ads: Advertising may be displayed on public pages and inside the authenticated application. Advertising is labelled and must not be clicked artificially. Some ads may open a sponsored page in a new tab; close it if you are not interested.
terms.liability: The service is provided as-is. We aim for high availability but do not guarantee uninterrupted access, and we are not liable for indirect losses arising from use of the service.
terms.contact: Questions about these terms can be sent using the address on the contact page.

contact.title: Contact
contact.intro: Use the address below for questions about {product}, account access, privacy requests or advertising.
contact.emailPlaceholder: Contact address to be published before launch.
contact.issues: If something looks wrong with your marks or bookings, contact your course staff first — they own the academic record. Report platform problems using the same address.
contact.ads: Advertising and sponsorship enquiries can use the same address. Never click ads on this site to test them; it violates the ad network's terms.

AdminAds.title: Ads administration
AdminAds.subtitle: Platform-level controls for ad placements, networks, kill switches and configuration versions. Every change writes an audit event and applies within seconds.
AdminAds.capability: Requires the platform.manage_ads capability (platform admins only).
AdminAds.flagsNote: Resolvers fail closed: a flag missing from feature_flags counts as off. ads.global_kill is checked before any kill-switch row.
AdminAds.killsNote: Precedence: ads.global_kill flag, then this global row, then per-network rows. Killing blocks ad units for every university; sponsor units are unaffected.
AdminAds.placementsNote: A placement serves an ad unit only while enabled, its page type is enabled (non-auth) and its network is enabled and not killed.
AdminAds.networksNote: Network script allowlists stay empty (ADR-008), so network units render as reserved empty boxes until scripts are enabled.
AdminAds.configNote: Publishing freezes the active registry as an immutable version; rollbacks append an old config as a new version (no in-place edits).

kills.globalHint: Blocks all network ad units platform-wide until released.
